cards.explanation: The answer is that they're destroying and scattering the sheep. That's the very first thing out of the LORD's mouth: "Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!" A shepherd's whole job is keeping the flock together and safe. These shepherds did the exact opposite.

The answer is False. The LORD says "…the sheep of My pasture!" in verse 1, and in verse 2 He calls them "My flock" and "My people." The sheep are His, friends. The shepherds were only tending what belonged to Him.

The answer is the shepherds themselves. Here's the turnaround, friends. The LORD says to the shepherds, "Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds…" They skipped attending to His flock, and now they're the ones getting attended to. Same word, very different delivery. Some attention you just don't want.

The answer is the LORD Himself. He doesn't hand this job to anybody else. The LORD says, "Then I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock from all the lands to which I have banished them…" The word is "Myself." The One who owns the flock goes out and gathers it.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…I will return them to their pasture, where they will be fruitful and multiply." He doesn't stop at gathering, friends. He brings them all the way home to their pasture. That's the whole trip, start to finish.

The answer is shepherds who will tend them. The LORD says it straight in verse 4: "I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them…" The job doesn't go away. He puts new shepherds in who will actually tend. Shepherds were never the problem, friends. Bad shepherding was.

The answer is False. The LORD says the flock "…will no longer be afraid or dismayed, nor will any go missing…" Not a few and not one. I once lost a spatula in a bakery the size of one cookie planet, so a flock with zero missing sounds like a miracle to me.

The answer is King. The LORD says, "…I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He will reign wisely as King…" So the word for the blank is King, friends. Reigning is exactly what the verse says the Branch will do.

The two words are saved and securely. The LORD says, "In His days Judah will be saved…" and then He says, "…Israel will dwell securely." Those are the two halves of the promise for when the righteous Branch reigns. Think of the flock earlier, scattered and afraid, friends. This is what the LORD promises for the Branch's days.

The name is The LORD Our Righteousness. The LORD says, "…this is His name by which He will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness." It comes right after the promise that Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell securely. Take it in slowly, friends, because this is a name worth sitting with.

The answer is bringing them back from the north. The people will say, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought and led the descendants of the house of Israel up out of the land of the north and all the other lands to which He had banished them." The old words about Egypt stay true, but this new rescue is the one they'll name. And it covers every land where He banished them, not only the north.
